LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 11.3.1 INTERROGATIVES

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.3: Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Interrogatives

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Interrogatives. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: when clauses with present tense to show the future, for example, ‘When are you going to school?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify interrogatives in print or digital texts
2. use interrogatives correctly to express different meanings

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: GRAMMAR IN USE 11.3.1 INTERROGATIVES
This lesson teaches Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Interrogatives for Grade 6 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

STUDY STEPS
1. identify interrogatives in print or digital texts
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
2. use interrogatives correctly to express different meanings
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Interrogatives using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Interrogatives above.
2. Explain Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Interrogatives to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Interrogatives.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Interrogatives with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Interrogatives important for a Grade 6 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. when clauses with present tense to show the future, for example, ‘When are you going to school?
2. How do you form questions?
3. Why do we ask questions?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify interrogatives in print or digital texts
2. use interrogatives correctly to express different meanings

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
